headline: 1 dead, 10 injured as bus overturns in Feni
summary: A customs official was killed and 10 others were injured when a passenger bus lost control and overturned at Lalpol, Feni Sadar.
details: A customs official was killed and 10 others were injured after a passenger bus overturned at Lalpol in Feni Sadar.
The accident occurred when the bus driver lost control of the vehicle after a truck ahead of them suddenly braked.
The victim, a customs official, was reportedly traveling to see a potential bride for marriage, but instead returned home as a body.
Emergency services responded to the scene to rescue the injured and transport them to the hospital.

headline: 481 lives lost in August road crashes in Bangladesh
summary: A Road Safety Foundation report reveals 513 accidents in August, with motorcycle crashes accounting for over 36% of the deaths.
details: A total of 481 people were killed and 664 injured in 513 road accidents across Bangladesh in August, according to a report by the Road Safety Foundation.
Motorcycle accidents were the deadliest, claiming 176 lives—roughly 36.59% of the total deaths. 183 motorcycles were involved in these crashes.
Pedestrians were the next most vulnerable group, with 102 deaths (21.20%), while 67 drivers and assistants were killed.
Breaking down the vehicle types, deaths included 78 three-wheeler passengers, 51 passengers from trucks and covered vans, 37 bus passengers, and 11 from private cars and jeeps.
A total of 749 vehicles were involved in the accidents throughout the month, including 194 motorcycles, 112 three-wheelers, 108 trucks, and 103 buses.
Beyond road crashes, the report also noted 6 deaths in 7 boat accidents and 27 deaths in 34 railway track accidents during the same period.
The Road Safety Foundation identified overspeeding and loss of vehicle control as the primary causes of most accidents.
Other contributing factors included reckless driving, faulty vehicles and roads, driver inefficiency, health issues, and poor traffic management.
caption:
481 people died in road accidents in August alone. Motorcycle crashes were the deadliest.

A total of 481 people were killed and 664 injured in 513 road accidents across Bangladesh in August, according to a report by the Road Safety Foundation.

Motorcycle accidents were the deadliest, claiming 176 lives—roughly 36.59% of the total deaths. 183 motorcycles were involved in these crashes.

Pedestrians were the next most vulnerable group, with 102 deaths (21.20%), while 67 drivers and assistants were killed.

Breaking down the vehicle types, deaths included 78 three-wheeler passengers, 51 passengers from trucks and covered vans, 37 bus passengers, and 11 from private cars and jeeps.

A total of 749 vehicles were involved in the accidents throughout the month, including 194 motorcycles, 112 three-wheelers, 108 trucks, and 103 buses.

Beyond road crashes, the report also noted 6 deaths in 7 boat accidents and 27 deaths in 34 railway track accidents during the same period.

The Road Safety Foundation identified overspeeding and loss of vehicle control as the primary causes of most accidents.

Other contributing factors included reckless driving, faulty vehicles and roads, driver inefficiency, health issues, and poor traffic management.
